Avoid 65%+ empty-space austerity (reads as cold and impersonal at bridge-premium). Equally avoid tight e-commerce-style layouts that compress space until nothing breathes. The 50–65% content ratio is the enforced range.
photography_direction: Documentary over directed: images must capture a moment or material in place — hands at work, fabric in natural light, a garment on a body mid-movement — not a constructed, symmetrical product shot. Perpendicular overhead angles, pure-white sweep backgrounds, and symmetrical centred compositions are prohibited.

Textural detail prioritised as primary brand communication: every editorial layout or product page must include at least one close-up shot of fabric grain, weave patterns, visible seam construction, or material surface (organic cotton thread, bamboo silk drape, fungi-based textile cross-section). These are not supporting imagery — they are primary visual content.

Shallow depth of field is acceptable only from a low angle or candid mid-scene framing. Cropped hands, partial frames, and real environmental edges (soil, unfinished wood, raw stone) are preferred over centred full-product isolation. Colour grading must remain warm and desaturated — no blue-grey shadows, no vibrancy boosting, no cooler-than-neutral temperature shifts.
report.materials: Uncoated, slightly rough-textured paper stock for all print. Matte or silk finish on photography reproduction — gloss finish is prohibited on all print and packaging. Embossing where used must be subtle and tactile, not deep or decorative. Printing registration may be intentionally soft to reinforce handmade quality. Deckle-edged paper or slightly soft trim is acceptable for packaging inserts and swing tags. All packaging materials must be visibly compostable or recycled-fibre, and this material quality must be communicated as part of the design — not hidden beneath overprinting.
do_rules: Use Raw Linen #EDE0CC as the default surface for every layout, screen background, and unprinted packaging field. Never use pure white (#FFFFFF) — it reads as clinical and over-processed.

Foreground material texture in every content piece: at least one image per editorial layout or product page must be a close-up textural detail — fabric grain, weave, hands, or material surface — not a full product shot or lifestyle editorial alone.
Limit the palette to exactly three colours per layout execution: Raw Linen #EDE0CC, Sage Green-Grey #7FAD9A, and Terracotta Sienna #C47C5A. No additional tones are introduced in any single execution.
Pair Lora display with Source Sans Pro body exclusively. This is the complete typographic system — one humanist serif with one humanist sans. No third typeface family under any circumstances.

Extend the brand visual system into all packaging touchpoints. Labels, swing tags, mailers, and tissue wrap carry the same palette, typography, and material logic as editorial and digital executions — packaging is brand communication, not a production afterthought.

Use Terracotta Sienna #C47C5A sparingly at a maximum of 15% of any layout surface, appearing only as a label edge, wayfinding sticker, single typographic headline, or textile detail accent. Never as a background fill.
dont_rules: Do not use high-gloss finishes on any print or packaging material. Gloss signals synthetic processing and directly contradicts the material-honesty positioning. Matte or uncoated stock only.

Do not use geometric sans-serif typefaces — including Futura display weights, Helvetica, and Montserrat as display — at any scale. Geometric sans reads as corporate modernism, the wrong temperature for this aesthetic.

Do not use high-saturation colours at any scale. No acid yellows, neon greens, or synthetic brights, even as small accent details. Any colour outside the defined three-colour palette reads as artificial and undermines the sustainability claim.

Do not use art-directed product photography with perpendicular overhead angles, pure-white sweep backgrounds, or symmetrical centred compositions. This codes as fast-fashion e-commerce or luxury minimalism — both are incorrect for bridge-premium craft positioning.

Do not introduce eco-labelling iconography or overt sustainability signage (recycling symbols, green-leaf badges, carbon-neutral stamps) into primary visual compositions. Sustainability is communicated through material texture, palette, and typography — not through label shorthand, which reads as greenwashing.

benchmark_brands.name: Stella McCartney SS25 'Designed for Tomorrow'
benchmark_brands.reference_note: Reference specifically for palette temperature: off-whites, warm taupes, and soft greens in editorial photography; how sustainability innovation is communicated through visual restraint rather than promotional loudness. Lift the colour temperature and negative space decisions, not the ultra-luxury austerity of margin width (their 70–75% empty-space ratio is too high for bridge-premium positioning).

benchmark_brands.name: PANGAIA 2025 Visual Refresh
benchmark_brands.reference_note: Reference specifically for how packaging design is integrated as primary brand communication with compostable materials as visual content, and how botanical and material storytelling appears in close-up texture photography. Also reference their humanist typography approach: clean, moderate tracking, never cold. Note: their lowercase wordmark and geometric sans trend signals are not adopted into the editorial type system.

benchmark_brands.name: Camila Machado / Mexican Artisanal Network (Vogue 'New Guard' feature)
benchmark_brands.reference_note: Reference specifically for the documentary, candid editorial photography approach and for how heritage craftsmanship — visible hand processes, organic textile origins — is framed with a minimal interventionist design hand. Study how this reference communicates artisanal authenticity without becoming decorative or nostalgic.

report.visual_narrative: This brand lives in the space between craft and confidence — it does not apologise for being sustainable, and it does not perform sustainability as a badge. Every layout starts with Raw Linen #EDE0CC: warm, unfinished, present. The camera gets close — to the weave, to the hands, to the grain of a fabric that has a provenance worth showing. Terracotta Sienna #C47C5A appears once, deliberately: a label edge, a single word, a sticker on compostable paper. Sage Green-Grey #7FAD9A holds the composition without letting warmth become sentimentality. Lora carries editorial headlines with the confidence of something printed and kept, not scrolled past. Source Sans Pro keeps body copy open and human. Nothing is gloss. Nothing is neon. Nothing shouts its ethics. The sustainability story is in the material — shown, not declared. Space breathes at 50–65%, generous enough to respect the product, grounded enough to stay accessible.
report.conflicts_resolved: CONFLICT 1 — Typography: Market trend signals lowercase wordmarks and tracking-heavy geometric sans-serif; theory specifies humanist serif display (Lora) paired with humanist sans body (Source Sans Pro). Resolution: Theory governs. The humanist pairing creates the warm, considered typographic voice required. Lowercase wordmark convention may be adopted at identity mark level only as a single concession — not extended to editorial typography. | CONFLICT 2 — Negative space ratio: Market trend references generous negative space as dominant; theory specifies a cap at 65% empty to avoid ultra-luxury austerity. Resolution: Theory governs with market nuance. The 50–65% content-to-space ratio honours the breathing-room signal while preventing the aesthetic from tipping into quiet-luxury territory inappropriate for bridge-premium pricing ($80–$400). Benchmark brands operating at 70–75% empty (Stella McCartney) are referenced for temperature, not margin ratios. | CONFLICT 3 — Colour: Market research introduces soft gold/ochre as accent signal; theory specifies Terracotta Sienna #C47C5A. Resolution: Theory governs on specific tone. Soft gold risks reading as precious or jewellery-adjacent, elevating tier perception beyond bridge-premium. Terracotta Sienna reads as earth pigment, not finish. The ochre signal from market trend is absorbed into photography direction (warm mid-morning light temperature) without introducing a fourth palette tone.
